What to try
  • Add 4 heads anywhere: the outflow uncertainty barely moves. Now add 4 K measurements.
  • Switch to “Best next location” for the outflow, with heads selected: the map stays almost empty. With K selected, it lights up.
  • Switch the target to “the conductivity field”: now heads become useful.
  • Place two K measurements very close together: the second adds little (redundancy).
How it works

200 random conductivity fields (all consistent with the same geostatistics) were run in MODFLOW 6. The spread of their results is the prior uncertainty. For any set of measurements, the remaining uncertainty is estimated with the linear data-worth formula, using covariances computed from the 200 runs:
Var(after) = Var(before) − Cov(prediction, data) · [Cov(data, data) + error]⁻¹ · Cov(data, prediction).
No measured values are needed: the formula tells you how much a measurement would help, before collecting it. It is a linear approximation (exact for K measurements, approximate for heads), and the map uses distance localization to remove spurious correlations from the finite ensemble.
